title: Check yourself: Thinking, computer use and when not to use a model

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A support tool runs its deepest reasoning setting on every request, including one-word intent labels. Spend is rising with no gain in quality. What does the documentation support as the first remedy?

options.text: Raise `max_tokens` so the reasoning always has room to finish
options.says: Ruled out because reasoning tokens "count toward max_tokens alongside the response text", so a larger cap only allows more spend.

options.text: Use low effort on trivial inputs and keep high effort for demanding ones
options.says: Thinking tokens are billed as output, so reserving them for tasks that benefit cuts the spend, and effort is the steering lever (the facts list and the first trap).

options.text: Move the labels to the model with the largest context window
options.says: Ruled out because the waste is in the reasoning: "Paying for reasoning on a one-word classification is waste", and a bigger window does not change that.

options.text: Switch to manual budgets everywhere, since adaptive thinking cannot be tuned
options.says: Ruled out because with adaptive thinking "the model decides how much to think, steered by effort", so it can be tuned without manual budgets.

questions.stem: A team must flag uploaded invoices issued within the past thirty days. Every entry carries a timestamp in one known format. Which design is best?

options.text: Ask Claude to judge each timestamp and pass the verdict through
options.says: Ruled out because "The model approximates; code is exact".

options.text: Ask Claude for each verdict at high effort so the date arithmetic is dependable
options.says: Ruled out because the table gives code as the answer for a one-line rule for the reason "Cheaper, faster, deterministic, testable", and a higher effort setting is none of those.

options.text: Give Claude a clock tool and have it compare each timestamp
options.says: Ruled out because the table sends "Anything that must happen every time" to a check in code, and a model comparing dates through a tool is still the model deciding.

options.text: Parse the field and compare it with today's date in code
options.says: A rule in a known format is code's job, cheaper, faster, deterministic and testable (the when-not-to table and the third trap).
